content: Phil Mynott News Collaboration Data AI for science expands to foundations and research institutions A news article by the Communication Team. 29 Oct 2026 Wellcome Sanger Institute partners with Anthropic on its AI for Science programme. Email newsletter News and blog updates Sign up Anthropic – an AI safety and research company – is highlighting 20 scientific foundations, institutions, and research groups from around the world who it has partnered with in an expansion of its AI for Science programme , which gives free Claude credits to researchers working on high-impact scientific projects. The Wellcome Sanger Institute is pleased to be partnering with Anthropic on AI for Science. The Institute’s discovery science will benefit from Anthropic’s AI-powered research platforms, which Sanger scientists will use to automate and accelerate complex computational biology and genomics analysis. Anthropic started the AI for Science programme a little over a year ago with the belief that AI could significantly accelerate and transform scientific progress. Its goal is to increase access to AI tools and resources in order to enable researchers to deepen and expand their own scientific work. (Over the last few months, Anthropic has also launched its discounted Team plan for scientists and has supported hundreds of projects across biology, medicine, physics, chemistry, climate science, and mathematics.) Scientists have said that they’re working with Claude to generate hypotheses, design experiments, swiftly analyse complex data, and communicate findings. By placing scientists at the centre of this transformation, the field is driving the questions and developing the research projects that will help Anthropic tackle some of humanity’s toughest problems. Over the past year, Anthropic has started to expand this work and partner with scientific organisations to build collaborative research projects. Now, Anthropic is sharing how this programme has further scaled up from supporting individual scientists to developing a large number of scientific partnerships with institutions and foundations to uplift researchers across a myriad of scientific fields. Many of these projects will also produce public goods that benefit the wider scientific community: open datasets, open-source software, open standards, and shared libraries. They look forward to seeing how AI resources can expand what scientists can attempt and lead to new discoveries. Science funders and societies Science funders and societies play an enormous role in finding and funding original, high-impact projects. Anthropic is sharing Claude credits with the following world-class foundations, who will distribute these resources to ambitious researchers aiming to use AI for scientific research: The Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. Founded in 1934, it supports original research and education in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and economics. The Simons Foundation. This foundation advances the frontiers of research in mathematics and basic sciences through grants and its Flatiron Institute. Schmidt Sciences. Founded in 2024 by Eric and Wendy Schmidt, it works to accelerate scientific knowledge and breakthroughs with the most promising, advanced tools to support a thriving planet. The organisation prioritises research in areas poised for impact including AI and advanced computing, astrophysics, biosciences, climate, and space—as well as supporting researchers in a variety of disciplines through its science systems program. Open Source for Science Fund, a program of Renaissance Philanthropy. This is a time-bound philanthropic fund at Renaissance Philanthropy sustaining and evolving the open source software stack that underpins science. The US National Science Foundation. This $9 billion federal agency established by Congress in 1950 promotes the progress of science, advances national health and defence, and funds competitive research and education, accounting for about 25 per cent of federal support for basic research at US colleges and universities. Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS), a division of the American Chemical Society. For more than a century, CAS has indexed the world’s published chemistry, and it maintains the CAS Registry, the standard system for identifying chemical substances. Institutions Leading research institutions produce some of the world’s most important scientific advances, data, instruments, and tools. These institutional partners will use Claude credits inside their organisations to enable scientific discovery: Space Telescope Science Institute. STScI runs science operations for NASA’s Hubble, James Webb, and Roman space telescopes. Managed by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA), STScI also holds one of the largest astronomy data archives used by scientists worldwide. Wellcome Sanger Institute.
